video_goal: Demonstrate the step-by-step process of replacing the cabin air filter in a Toyota RAV4 (XA50) to restore optimal HVAC airflow.
single_prompt: Demonstrate the step-by-step process of replacing the cabin air filter in a Toyota RAV4 (XA50) to restore optimal HVAC airflow. From a first-person view, a hand opens the passenger side door of a Toyota RAV4 (XA50), revealing the dashboard and closed glovebox. From an over-the-shoulder view, a hand presses the glovebox latch button and lowers the glovebox door to the open position. In a close-up, fingers pinch the black plastic damper rod located on the right exterior side of the glovebox and slide it outward off its mounting peg. In a medium shot, two hands press inward on both outer edges of the glovebox simultaneously to clear the plastic stopper tabs from the dashboard frame. The glovebox swings downward toward the floorboards, exposing the black plastic HVAC blower unit hidden behind the dash. The camera zooms in on the rectangular cabin air filter cover on the HVAC unit, highlighting the 'UP' arrow molded into the plastic. A thumb and index finger squeeze the release clip on the right side of the filter cover and pull the cover completely off. A hand reaches into the exposed slot and pulls out a dark grey, debris-filled pleated cabin air filter. From a top-down view, the dirty grey filter is placed side-by-side on the floor mat next to a pristine, bright white new cabin air filter. In a close-up, fingers point to the printed 'UP' arrow and airflow indicator on the side of the new white filter. From an over-the-shoulder view, a hand slides the new white filter horizontally into the empty HVAC slot until it sits completely flush inside the unit. In a close-up, a hand aligns the left side of the plastic filter cover into its groove, then pushes the right side until the clip snaps securely into place. In a medium shot, two hands lift the glovebox upward, pushing firmly until the side stopper tabs pop back behind the dashboard frame. Finally, in a close-up, fingers slide the black damper rod back onto the side peg of the glovebox, then push the glovebox completely shut.
